facts.heading: Anxiety worsens in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Deputy Head role
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school. She has taught there for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years and i love it.

facts.heading: Asked to step up role
facts.content: Hannah was asked to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: And then had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking people picked the wrong person. She fears someone will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person. And that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Nighttime rehearsal thoughts
facts.content: Mostly on Sunday evenings, Hannah's chest tightens and she rehearses Monday's meetings in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings my chest goes tight and i start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential questions
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question someone might ask and what she would say and what they would think of her if she got it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what i would say and what they would think of me if i got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of perceived incompetence
facts.content: Hannah fears Mr. Hargraves will think she is stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Email rewriting behavior policy
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governor's four times. The email was about the behavior policy and was two paragraphs long.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governor's four times. Uh, changed to the behavior policy. It was two paragraphs.

facts.heading: Governor's reaction to Hannah
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah. He was delighted when he talked to her in September.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He talked me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of lying to Governor
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable.
facts.evidence: That makes it worse somehow because i feel like i'm lying to him. About being capable as if i'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feeling like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat most days.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a head teacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy in village
facts.content: Everyone in the village still mentions Hannah's mother as a wonderful head teacher.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me, say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother retired six years ago
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago. A library has been named after her.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and i should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Mother's comments impact Hannah
facts.content: When her mother says this, Hannah feels like she is making a fuss so she doesn't tell.
facts.evidence: How does it land when she says that? It makes me feel like i'm making a fuss so i don't tell

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at four every morning. I fall sleep fine. Then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Drinking coffee to cope
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through her mornings. This has been happening since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term I drink a lot of coffee to get through it today

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: During the afternoons, Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Exhaustion from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted at the end of every day due to pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice on feelings
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben suggests she should just enjoy things.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: When Ben suggests she enjoy things, Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Relationship with friends changed
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends at school who have talked to her recently.
facts.evidence: Not anymore. Not really.

facts.heading: Shift in social role
facts.content: Hannah is now the line manager and talks for the students.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and I talk for it.

facts.heading: Missing past school life
facts.content: Hannah misses her class and the children most.
facts.evidence: I missed them. I missed my class too. They live a bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Regret about leaving school
facts.content: Hannah regrets not going back to school.
facts.evidence: And I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Lack of external support
facts.content: No one has asked Hannah a deeper question about her feelings.
facts.evidence: Nobody has asked me that. They just say, well done.

facts.heading: Relaxation during holidays
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during summer holidays when she did not think about school for ten days.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays, we went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Difference during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just talking, then carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Difficulty eating before term
facts.content: Hannah could not eat on the sundry the week before a term.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the sundry

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening

facts.heading: Writing down stopped after two weeks
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly

facts.heading: Feeling silly about writing
facts.content: Hannah felt silly when writing in a notebook.
facts.evidence: As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook

facts.heading: Desire to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud

facts.heading: Goal for meeting behavior
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing and send only one email.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first, sending an email once

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening calm
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa without stomach knots on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots

facts.heading: Feeling about stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light, lighter, and a bit tearful when saying goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful actually

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben about 4am
facts.content: Hannah is afraid to tell Ben how bad things are.
facts.evidence: Not even Ben knows how about the 4am

facts.heading: Fear of Ben's reaction
facts.content: Hannah fears Ben would be hurt if she told him sooner.
facts.evidence: He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner

facts.heading: Choosing a quiet moment to tell
facts.content: Hannah thinks choosing a quiet moment helps her tell someone.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up

facts.heading: Planning to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah plans to try the evening notebook again for a week.
facts.evidence: I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget
